annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Not a truant, but the-sort that attend for long.' reads as garbled OCR: the sense needs a negative (the sort that cannot attend for long), which is missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Not a truant, but the-sort that attend for long.

clue.text: It must be a plant, Tom here in dition.!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'It must be a plant, Tom here in dition.!' is garbled OCR; the wordplay beyond Tom = CAT cannot be recovered with confidence.
annotationWithheld.clue: It must be a plant, Tom here in dition.!

clue.text: This may well be a fine old yarn.

definitions.text: This may well be a fine old yarn.

parts.words: This may well be a fine old yarn
parts.note: a yarn is a story, and a fine old story handed down through generations is the custom passed from parent to child

explanation.surface: Someone praising a good old story.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs and beliefs handed down over generations often survive as old tales, so a venerable story fits the word.

clue.text: Windy Greek? No, a lie perhaps.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the preceding words might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: taken as written, the words no and a lie supply the six letters

explanation.surface: Is that Greek a windbag? No, the claim is a falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges NO A LIE. The word means both 'of the wind' (after Aeolus, Greek god of the winds) and 'of the Aeolian Greeks', so 'Windy Greek' covers both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from Aeolus, keeper of the winds, and also names an ancient Greek people of Aeolis.

clue.text: Gun platform with a jagged top.

definitions.text: Gun platform with a jagged top.

parts.words: Gun platform with a jagged top
parts.note: a raised mound or platform from which guns fire over a parapet; the jagged top hints at a barb, a sharp hooked point, at the word's start

explanation.surface: A description of a fortification with a rough upper edge.
explanation.definitionFit: In fortification this is the raised earthwork or turret from which cannon fire over the wall.

clue.text: How a fool may turn up, but distant.

indicators.note: to turn something up can mean to churn it over, so the letters of the phrase are shuffled

explanation.surface: A clown might appear unexpectedly yet stay remote.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turn up' tempts a reversal, but A FOOL backwards is LOOFA; it is an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone remote and reserved in manner keeps others at a distance, a synonym for standoffish.

clue.text: Counter treatment of a lie in some shop?

definitions.text: Counter treatment of a lie in some shop?

parts.words: Counter treatment of a lie in some shop
parts.note: shopkeepers once fixed fake coins to the counter with a spike; to do the same to a falsehood is to expose it once and for all

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper dealing with a dishonest customer at the till.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'nail a lie to the counter' is an old idiom for exposing it, from the practice of spiking counterfeit coins to a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing a falsehood decisively is the idiom of pinning it down so it can circulate no further.

clue.text: Find no aged men right — a most ungenerous role.

indicators.note: the solver is told to find a new word in the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Searching for an elderly man who is correct, in an unkind part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' asks for the fourteen letters of NO AGED MEN RIGHT to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The fable's dog keeps the oxen from hay it cannot eat itself, so the phrase names a spiteful, ungenerous person.

clue.text: Procedure which involves an outsider in work with an olive-branch.

definitions.text: Procedure which involves an outsider in work with an olive-branch.

parts.words: Procedure which involves an outsider in work with an olive-branch
parts.note: a neutral third party steps into a dispute carrying the emblem of peace to bring the sides together

explanation.surface: A description of a peace process run by a stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting as go-between in a quarrel, an outsider offering peace terms, is what a mediator does.

clue.text: What any forward hopes to do — in game!

definitions.text: What any forward hopes to do
definitions.meaning: an attacking player wants to put the ball into the goal's mesh
a team sport played mostly by women with a high hoop

explanation.surface: A striker's ambition during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it is the striker's aim; as one it is the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport played with a high ring, and the phrase for sending the ball into the mesh.

clue.text: Top class of cover, this.

parts.note: the covering at the very top of a building, such as slates or tiles, rather than first-rate quality

explanation.surface: Boasting of first-rate insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Material laid over the top of a house, such as tiles or thatch, is literally its highest covering.

clue.text: Effect one type of knock-out.

parts.note: in a cup competition losing teams are knocked out, so causing such an exit is a kind of knock-out

explanation.surface: A boxing instruction to land a decisive blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing a competitor from a tournament is exactly what a knock-out round does.

clue.text: What life ignoble hides to make pretence.

indicators.note: the phrase life ignoble conceals a run of letters across its two words

explanation.surface: An ignoble existence masks a sham.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend or simulate is the usual synonym, as in faking illness.

clue.text: Brief examination before entrance.

parts.note: a shortened name for the old school-leaving test that qualified pupils for university entry

explanation.surface: A quick check before someone is let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' says the word is a shortening, of matriculation, the old British exam for university entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: The clipped form of matriculation, an examination taken for admission to university.

clue.text: "Man's" (Kipling.)

parts.note: a fill-in quotation: the missing word follows Man's in a line by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: A quotation from Kipling with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Old crosswords often used gap-fill quotations: the answer completes the quoted phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted phrase about a man's might is completed by this word for power.

clue.text: Choice functions might one call them?.

definitions.text: Choice functions might one call them?

parts.words: Choice functions might one call them
parts.note: events where voters make their choice are polls, and one might call them functions of choosing

explanation.surface: Asking whether some select social events have a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Polls at which voters choose representatives are, literally, occasions for choosing.

clue.text: What to do when answering a call.

definitions.text: What to do when answering a call.

parts.words: What to do when answering a call
parts.note: a performer answering a curtain call comes back on stage

explanation.surface: Advice on replying to a phone ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: Responding to a curtain call means coming back into view of the audience.

clue.text: Unearth some obscure affair.

parts.note: to dig up from the ground, and figuratively to bring a forgotten matter back to light

explanation.surface: An investigator digging up a forgotten scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Digging a body out of a grave is the literal sense; reviving a buried matter the figurative one.

clue.text: Bowl over.

parts.note: knock down, as pins are sent flying by a rolled ball

explanation.surface: Astonish someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To send pins flying, and by extension to knock anything down, is to topple it.

clue.text: Ambled about in a madhouse!

indicators.note: about here means the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone strolled around inside an asylum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges AMBLED; the answer was the popular name of Bethlem asylum in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The old London hospital for the insane gave its nickname to any scene of uproar or lunatic asylum.

clue.text: The old rascal, including a politician in a personal attack!

indicators.note: including means the word for a rascal takes the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: loon is an old word for a rogue or idler
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A satirical swipe at a crooked old MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A satire ridiculing a particular person is a mocking personal attack.

clue.text: Apple with apparently a very soft core.

definitions.text: Apple with apparently a very soft core.

parts.words: Apple with apparently a very soft core
parts.note: in music pp means very soft, and those letters sit at the centre of the apple variety's name

explanation.surface: A fruit whose middle seems mushy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pp' (pianissimo) is the musical mark for very soft; the apple's name has it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety of eating apple grown from seed, as in Cox's Orange.

clue.text: An impatient cry — just like that monkey!

parts.note: pish is an old exclamation of contempt or impatience

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming in irritation that a person resembles a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means resembling a primate such as a monkey, imitative in manner.

clue.text: One of those favourite resorts.

parts.note: a place someone visits often, rather than a holiday destination

explanation.surface: A popular seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: A place frequented habitually by someone, a regular spot.

clue.text: One may be found in maps not sorted.

definitions.text: One may be found in maps not sorted.

indicators.note: sorted tells the solver the letters of the phrase are put into a different order

explanation.surface: An official appears among some unfiled charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted' rearranges IN MAPS NOT. A pointsman is a railwayman who works the points, the movable rails that switch trains between tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway worker in charge of the switches, or a traffic policeman on duty at a junction.

clue.text: Paul Pry was very apt to.

definitions.text: Paul Pry was very apt to.

parts.words: Paul Pry was very apt to
parts.note: Paul Pry, the nosy hero of an 1825 comedy, kept turning up uninvited with an apologetic catchphrase

explanation.surface: Remarking on a nosy man's habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Pry's catchphrase was 'I hope I don't intrude', so his name became a byword for a busybody.
explanation.definitionFit: Barging in where one is not wanted is the busybody's habit, forcing oneself on others.

clue.text: " Why don't the men — the men" (Bayly.)

definitions.text: " Why don't the men — the men" (Bayly.)

parts.words: " Why don't the men — the men" (Bayly.)
parts.note: a gap-fill line from the song by Thomas Haynes Bayly lamenting that men never ask for a hand in marriage

explanation.surface: A quotation from a Victorian song with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking a woman to marry is the sense needed in the songwriter's line about bashful suitors.

clue.text: Big, fine offspring — well, so one hopes.

definitions.text: Big, fine offspring — well, so one hopes.

parts.note: great means big
grand means fine or splendid
sons are male offspring

explanation.surface: A grandparent hoping their descendants turn out large and splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Male descendants two generations below one's children, whom an elderly person might hope to see.
